questions.question: What happened when Moses threw his shepherd's staff on the ground?
options: It turned into a tree branch.
It turned into a snake and then disappeared.
It turned into a snake, and then back into a staff when he grabbed its tail.
It turned into a stone.
questions.explanation: According to verses 3-4, the staff turned into a snake when thrown down, and then back into a staff when Moses grabbed its tail.

questions.question: What was Moses's initial concern about going to the Israelites?
options: He was worried they wouldn't believe the Lord had appeared to him.
He felt he wasn't good with words.
He was afraid of Pharaoh.
He didn't want to leave his father-in-law, Jethro.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 states Moses's concern: 'What if they won’t believe me or listen to me? What if they say, ‘The Lord never appeared to you’?'

questions.question: What was the second miraculous sign the Lord showed Moses?
options: His staff turning into a snake.
His hand becoming white with a severe skin disease and then healthy again.
Water from the Nile turning to blood.
Aaron appearing to meet him in the wilderness.
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 describe the second sign: Moses's hand became 'white as snow with a severe skin disease' and then was restored to health.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'a bridegroom of blood' refer to in the passage?
options: Moses's marriage to Zipporah.
The Lord's anger with Moses.
The act of circumcision performed by Zipporah.
The blood of the firstborn son.
questions.explanation: Verse 26 clarifies that when Zipporah said 'a bridegroom of blood,' 'she was referring to the circumcision.'

questions.question: Who did the Lord appoint to be Moses's spokesman to the people?
options: Jethro, his father-in-law.
One of Moses's sons.
Aaron, his brother.
Moses himself, after God instructed him.
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 16 state that the Lord designated Aaron, Moses's brother, saying, 'Aaron will be your spokesman to the people.'
